fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. The verse says, “…you do not need anyone to write to you, because you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another.” So the reason they don't need a letter about it is that God had taught them. That's the answer, and it's a good one to land on.
Yep. Paul and his companions say it right to them: “This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.” That's a compliment before the ask. Friend, I'd hang that one on my bakery wall.

The letter says the opposite. Paul and his companions say, “This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.” So they get a compliment first and a nudge second. Nobody is being scolded here, friend.
That's it. The verse says, “…each of you must know how to control his own body in holiness and honor…” That's each of you, friend. Nobody is left out of this one.
The verse says otherwise. They write that the Lord will avenge all such acts, “…as we have already told you and solemnly warned you.” So this is a repeat, and they'd been warned before, friend.
The verse says the opposite: “…you do not need anyone to write to you…” Then comes the reason, which is that they've been taught by God to love one another. That's a good thing to hear, friend.
The Law isn't mentioned in these verses. The reason is that they “…have been taught by God to love one another.” God was their teacher, friend.
Galatia isn't the place named here. The verse says they show love “…to all the brothers throughout Macedonia.” Macedonia is the answer, friend.
Judea isn't the place named here. It says, “And you are indeed showing this love to all the brothers throughout Macedonia.” So the answer is Macedonia, friend.

Travel isn't on the list. The verse says to “…aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands…” Those are the three things named. Sounds like a quiet life and some hard work, friend.
